newsitem.title: USA: Fed questions umbrella supervision in some cases.
newsitem.headline: Fed questions umbrella supervision in some cases.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday questioned the need for unbrella supervision of a holding company in which a bank was a minor factor.

In testimony before a House Banking subcommittee, Greenspan said that should Congress widen activities for financial services holding companies, it should recognize that such a bank can be protected adequately through bank capital requirements and existing Fed powers.

"The case is weak, in our judgement, for umbrella supervision of a holding company in which the bank is not the dominant unit and is not large enough to induce systemic problems should it fail," he said.

He made clear that the Fed was not taking a position on what activities holding companies with commercial operations can undertake, as long as it did not hamper its ability to deal with crisis and pursue monetary policy.

But even though it was not interested in closely regulating smaller institutions as such, he did argue that a significant sampling of smaller banks would be useful "so we have a sense of what the market is doing."
